correctness.rationale: On acute scalene faces, [2] proves precisely four rigid octahedral realizations. For each twisted realization its coordinates yield p²=R+d², q²=R+e², s²=2R+(e-d)², and volume 2R(d+e)/3. The coordinate octahedron has squared half-axes de, R+e(e-d), R+d(d-e), all positive under acuteness. Subtraction yields exactly (4/9)(d-e)²(R-2de)². In the scalene case d≠e; R=2de forces s longest and yields the stated complete equality family. All faces share the same area, symmetry makes the origin equidistant from them, and the zero sum of eight unit outward normals proves this is the unique maximal inball, with V=8Δρ/3. A rational arithmetic checker passed 728 feasible instances and exhaustively found nine cube perfect matchings in four partitions; finite checks corroborate, not replace, universal proof.

value.rationale: All four realizations have the identical eight triangular facets and surface area; minimizing their Euclidean volume/inradius is a natural metric extremal question not determined by class enumeration. The exact nonnegative perfect-square gap gives a sharp all-parameter minimum and a rigid exceptional continuum of two noncongruent minimizers. The explicit (√5,2√2,3) example has both arrangements with surface area 24, volume 8 and inradius 1. This is a structural classification with a surprising nonuniqueness boundary, not a routine numerical lookup or arbitrary invariant.
